prompt: Why are B+ trees preferred over standard Binary Search Trees or Hash Indexes for relational database table indexing?
options: B+ trees require O(1) time for all operations
B+ trees eliminate the need for write-ahead logging
B+ trees use less memory than hash tables for point lookups
B+ trees keep data in sorted leaf nodes linked sequentially, enabling efficient range scans and high-fanout shallow disk I/O
explanation: Disk I/O is costly; B+ trees have high branching factor (fanout > 100), meaning tree depth is typically 3-4. All records are stored at leaf level in linked order, making range queries (`BETWEEN a AND b`) efficient.
